It's the original page in the browser that has the ability to show ads and tell YouTube a user has watched a video. So to show a YouTube video the way that you want, one of two things is needed. 

A) a native YouTube player for VRChat, or maybe Unity programs in general

B) the video player needs to switch to being a browser somehow embedded into VRChat. There used to be a web panel, but it was removed after security issues and I suspect the creator of the package is doing other things these days. Using a browser like this would make sync very difficult.

Trying to sync YouTube videos with ad breaks could be impossible.

What I've seen in logs is that yt-dlp takes a video page link and gives VRChat a URL to a mp4 file that is then streamed. But there is no YouTube page running to report a view.

If YouTube were to provide a player for unity that handles the ads breaks nicely (hold the video for everyone) I could see it at least being used, but I guess part of the trouble is that world are using YouTube to host background music.

details:
VRChat video players will normally download the video/stream onto the disk to then play. This has been the default behavior for years now.

However this has many issues:

-Can eventually lead to legal issues with youtube(or get vrc/users blocked)

-Lag(Videos are more dependent on hardware and connection to vrchat servers instead of youtube, causing problems on some hardwares, lag, etc)

-Wont count as views for the video/stream(Many times I've seen streams with 5 viewers being displayed to maybe 30 people, but twitch/youtube doesnt count it because vrchat is downloading it instead of embedding) which is unfair to the creator

-won't display ads(and I know, ads suck, but thats how content creators make a living and how things are possible to be Free on the internet)

-etc

My suggestion: Instead of downloading, embed the video/stream from the original page onto the game.
title: Embed videos/streams instead of downloading
